Waterloo Regional Police Services - 2025 Budget Presentation
notes:
Ian Mclean, Chair, Waterloo Region Police Services Board, introduced a presentation on the Waterloo Region Police Service budget and business plan from 2024-2027. Mark Crowell, Chief, Waterloo Regional Police Service (WRPS), elaborated on crime statistics in Waterloo Region which informed the budget process for 2025. He further expanded on the various projects and other involvement that WRPS has been a part of within the Region. M. Crowell also provided a description of the staffing and hiring practices and related highlights for WRPS. Kirsten Hand, Director of Finance, WRPS, provided an overview on the budget drivers, operating estimate considerations, and the capital budget for 2025.

In reply to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell explained the necessity of health benefits costs as it relates to the police service, which experience significant trauma events. K. Hand further described the details of costs associated with health benefits and long-term disability. She acknowledged the stress that the current economic conditions are having on budgets for police services and WRPS's efforts in ensuring sustainable finances.

Responding to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell spoke to the efforts that WRPS is undertaking to be proactive in their service to the community, including the community safety wellbeing plan, the crisis diversion program, the impact program, and the alternative destination model. He elaborated on the critical efforts towards improving mental health responses and highlighted the need for various opportunities to be pursued to enhance these types of calls. As it pertains community groups, he explained that there are partnerships in place with community groups, including those to focus on the priority of Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls, as well as the implementation of the Reconciliation Action plan within WRPS.

In response to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell explained the core responsibilities associated with the Police Act that are reflected in the community and safety wellbeing plan. He further answered that the role of special constables is evolving, and that with any changes in the organization, overall changes are looked at. He elaborated on the details of deployment of special constables; however, the landscape of the role's responsibilities and wage is changing, which the WRPS is paying attention to. M. Crowell indicated the WRPS is looking at the KPMG recommendation which speaks to reconfiguring the special constable role.

Replying to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell answered that the WRPS is extensively in favour of call diversion where possible to be more sustainable with resources. M. Crowell answered that there are changes being made to emergency calls to account for assistance with mental health crises, and that more discussion could be happening at the provincial level to enhance mental health response services.

In reply to questions from the Committee, M. Crowell explained that an increase in hate crime could be attributed to societal polarization, and that the WRPS is taking action to address these issues and provide support for those victimized by hate crime. M. Crowell noted the complexity in reporting hate crimes, and that WRPS does try to account for other types of hate crime, including looking at hate-motivated incidents. He also spoke to the issue of intimate partner violence, and that community partners will confirm that supportive agencies are being reached out to. 

Responding to a question from the Committee, K. Hand commented on the unfunded liabilities in the budget, one being the sick leave reserve which has been actioned on, and the other being the future employee benefits which has also been actioned on through collective bargaining, as well as the implementation of a new reserve. M. Crowell spoke to shared funding attempts with other municipalities to mitigate costs.

In response to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell spoke in support of the direction of the Region as it relates to Municipal Speed Cameras and automated speed enforcement as a supplement, but not substitute, to other traffic calming measures. WRPS will seek to reduce fatalities on roadways including through collaboration with municipalities.

Replying to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell answered that the WRPS has sought to modernize data reporting, and it is his belief that WRPS is being transparent. He provided an overview on how overtime hours impact hiring practices and budgeting, which are related to the complexity of accounting for overtime in frontline duties; this also impacts civilian hires.

In reply to a question from the Committee, M. Crowell indicated that there are streams of funding and advocacy for the Family Violence Project and other supports including from the Solicitor General.
